title: A map of sheaves on a topological space is surjective iff it is surjective on stalks
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space (this node is about sheaves on the space $X$ itself, e.g. the Zariski topology of a scheme; not about the étale site) and $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ a morphism of presheaves of sets on $X$. Then the following are equivalent: (a) $\varphi$ is surjective in the sense of sheaves, i.e. for every open $U\subseteq X$ and every $t\in\mathcal G(U)$ there is an open covering $U=\bigcup_kU_k$ such that each $t|_{U_k}$ lies in the image of $\varphi_{U_k}:\mathcal F(U_k)\to\mathcal G(U_k)$; (b) for every $x\in X$ the induced map on stalks $\varphi_x:\mathcal F_x\to\mathcal G_x$ is surjective. The same holds for presheaves of abelian groups or of modules, by applying it to the underlying presheaves of sets (stalks and surjectivity are those of the underlying sets).
